title: Al-Qahhar, the Subduer
hookLine: the Subduer, over whom nothing prevails
tomorrow: Jordan's grandma gave them paint and wants nothing back. why?

cards: Some problems arrive as a form: a permit, a lease, a sign-off from someone you'll never meet. Amira's wall just got one. The building's owner has to approve the mural, and nobody knows when he'll answer, or if.
Yesterday asked: now what? The Qur'an has a man with a far bigger wall in front of him. His name is Yusuf, the same name as Amira's dad, and he's in prison for something he didn't do.

teach.b: Yusuf has every reason to think the prison is the strongest thing in his life.

Instead, he turns to the two men locked up with him and asks, in Pickthall's words: "O my two fellow-prisoners! Are divers lords better, or Allah the One, the Almighty?" That last word is today's name.
Al-Qahhar: the Subduer, the One over whom nothing prevails. Pickthall renders it the Almighty. Not the guards, not the king, not the walls.
Notice what Yusuf does and doesn't do. He doesn't pretend the cell isn't real. He keeps being himself inside it: he listens, he explains dreams, he asks to be remembered to the king.
He does his part, and leaves the part he can't move to the One nothing prevails over. The tradition gives this week a short line for the same balance.
A man asked the Prophet, peace be upon him, whether to tie his camel or trust Allah, and the answer, in paraphrase from Tirmidhi: tie it, and trust.
And the Qur'an adds a promise about size: "Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope." So here's the thing to say to a friend tonight: the too-big thing is real, and so is the One who is bigger.
Your job is the rope on the camel. The rest isn't on your back.

how: Muslims speak of tawakkul, trust in Allah alongside effort, and the 'tie your camel' hadith is one way it's taught; in the Qur'an al-Qahhar is paired with 'the One'.

o: the One who wins each argument with words
the One over whom nothing at all prevails
the One who punishes every wrong at once

games.q: Yusuf in prison — tap the pairs.
p: what Allah doesn't task a soul with

s: trusting Allah means you stop doing anything about the problem
tie the camel, and trust. Yusuf kept doing his part inside the cell.
Yusuf names al-Qahhar while he's still in prison
he asks his fellow-prisoners: divers lords, or Allah the One, the Almighty?
Pickthall renders al-Qahhar in that verse as 'the Almighty'
Allah the One, the Almighty: the One over whom nothing prevails.

games.q: your family's lease renewal is stuck with a landlord who won't reply. what does today's teaching suggest first?
o: do the part that's yours, one clear message, then set the rest down.
do nothing at all; if it's meant to work out, it will by itself.
message every day until he answers; it's all on you to force it.
games.why: tie the camel, and trust. effort and trust together, the way Yusuf did his part inside the prison and left the walls to al-Qahhar.

practice: On a scrap of paper, write the thing that feels too big this week in a few words. Fold it once and set it face down beside you. For the sit, keep your hands open and empty in your lap, and let it lie there, put down for now.

wordCard.voice: Al-Qahhar: the Subduer, the One over whom nothing prevails. Yusuf named Him from inside a prison cell.

orig.note: Arabic: the Subduer, over whom nothing prevails. in Yusuf's question in surah 12.

carryVoice: For the road: nothing prevails over him, so tie the rope and set the rest down. See you tomorrow.
